### What problem does this PR solve?

Issue Number: close #24951, #25186, #25183 <!-- REMOVE this line if no issue to close -->

Problem Summary

- Fix the issue of "Updating date returns an error after or during conversion `timestamp` to `date`".
- Make `TestChangingColOriginDefaultValue` meaningful.

### What is changed and how it works?

How it Works:

- Set the `OriginDefaultValue` back after finishing `changing column type`.
- Make `update stmt's` plan in `TestChangingColOriginDefaultValue` is `point get`.


### Check List <!--REMOVE the items that are not applicable-->

Tests <!-- At least one of them must be included. -->

- Unit test

### Release note <!-- bugfixes or new feature need a release note -->

- Fix update date returning an error after or during conversion `timestamp` to `date`.

issue_context.title: Updating date  return an error after  conversion `timestamp` to `date`
issue_context.body:
## Bug Report

Please answer these questions before submitting your issue. Thanks!
TiDB need to `set set global tidb_enable_change_column_type = 1;`

### 1. Minimal reproduce step (Required)

<!-- a step by step guide for reproducing the bug. -->
```
drop table tbl_41;
create table tbl_41 (col timestamp default '1971-06-09' not null);
alter table tbl_41 modify column col date not null;
update tbl_41 set col = '2002-12-31';
```

### 2. What did you expect to see? (Required)
`Query OK, 0 rows affected (0.00 sec)`

### 3. What did you see instead (Required)
`ERROR 1292 (22007): Incorrect date value: '0000-00-00'`

### 4. What is your TiDB version? (Required)

<!-- Paste the output of SELECT tidb_version() -->
```
Release Version: v4.0.0-beta.2-2957-g4000975ad
Edition: Community
Git Commit Hash: 4000975ad1785fbc4c0e5175407e8486c0cef763
Git Branch: master
```
comments:
Due to https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/7f4f5c02364b6578da561ec14f409a39ddf954a5/ddl/column.go#L853
It will set zero original default value, and the default value for `date` type is `0000-00-00`.
After  ```alter table tbl_41 modify column col date not null;```
the OriginDefaultValue of `tbl_41` will become `0000-00-00`.

How can I fix it?
Change the default value not zero seems feasible.

```
prior 1: if new col has its default value, using it as the origin-default value.

prior 3: use the zero value (partial logic in `generateOriginDefaultValue`) 
```
